title: Consolidate networking Terraform workspaces into a single modular surface
text:
Consolidate networking Terraform workspaces into a single modular surface

description:
Problem: We have multiple near-duplicate Terraform networking templates and per-environment workspaces that diverged over time (stage/production/ci). This causes long plan/apply times, repeated drift work, and frequent provider-version conflicts during concurrent changes. Goal: Collapse the duplicated networking templates into a single parameterized module surface, standardize workspace usage, and upgrade the AWS provider to a constrained version range that is compatible with the new module interfaces. Deliverables: 1) new central networking module with clear inputs/outputs for VPC, subnets, route tables, and EIP lifecycle; 2) migration runbook and automated state moves for affected workspaces; 3) CI pipeline changes to enforce provider pins and run acceptance tests; 4) a rollback plan and canary migration for two non-critical regions before production-wide migration.

acceptance_criteria:
Central networking module lives in terraform/modules/networking and is consumed by all env overlays
All existing workspace plans for stage/production/ci produce no diff after migration (besides expected renames)
AWS provider pinned to ~> 5.18 and documented compatibility notes for 5.16-5.20
State migrations executed via automated CI job with pre/post validation checks
Plan time for network stack reduced by >=25% in stage during rollout

tech_notes:
We will adopt workspace-aware module variables instead of duplicating template files per workspace.
Primary provider bump target: 5.18.0 — chosen for compatibility with existing EIP lifecycle behavior and provider schema changes introduced in 5.17.
Retain a provider alias strategy for cross-account resources to minimize large-scale refactoring in account-scoped modules.
Prefer explicit resource renaming (terraform state mv) over rewrite when resource addresses change; keep a mapping spreadsheet in Confluence.
Plan to add lightweight acceptance tests using Terratest (Go) for VPC/subnet/cidr/name collisions triggered in CI per-PR.
We will not introduce Terragrunt in this cycle — keep changes limited to Terraform core and module surfaces to reduce blast radius.

migration_plan:
1) Create new module and test in a disposable AWS account overlay with same workspace naming convention.
2) Run terraform plan in parallel for stage region to determine address differences (generate mapping).
3) Create CI job that performs terraform state mv commands against a read-only snapshot and validates plan produces no unexpected changes.
4) Perform canary migration for 'eu-west-1-staging' during low-traffic window; apply and verify routing/peering and EIP behavior.
5) If canary is successful for 48 hours, schedule automated migrations for remaining regions in rolling batches with 2-hour verification windows.
6) After full migration, retire old templates and add deprecation notes to repo and infra docs.

rollback_plan:
If canary shows regressions: immediate terraform apply using previous module version from snapshot branch to revert to pre-migration state.
Maintain snapshots of tfstate and configuration in the secure bucket for 30 days to allow state restore.
Open incident with SRE on-call and escalate to platform lead if route table or peering faults impact production traffic.
Documentation: include exact terraform state mv reverse commands in runbook so rollbacks are reproducible.

comments:
2025-02-19 — Aisha Patel: Initial triage: cataloged 7 duplicated networking templates across 3 accounts. Created migration spreadsheet and counted ~240 managed resources per env that will need address mapping.
2025-02-25 — Marco Chen: Completed prototype module for VPC/subnets. Observed plan time drop ~28% in local test account. Need to iron out route table naming differences with existing overlays.
2025-02-27 — Priya Nair (Infra Security): Security review requested. Confirmed cross-account IAM roles used for state operations meet least-privilege requirements; asked for KMS key ARN documentation for tfstate bucket.
2025-03-01 — Design review (Luca Romano): Asked for tags parity across environments (owner, cost-center, lifecycle) to avoid drift. Added tagging matrix to module defaults.
2025-03-02 — Marco Chen: Opening RFC PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/2141 — includes module code, acceptance tests, and CI workflow changes. Seeking 2 approvals before canary.
2025-03-03 — Aisha Patel: Blocker note: provider upgrade exposes a minor behavior change in elastic IP 'reassociation' logic on 5.19. Added compatibility shim to module and included detailed test case. Planning canary for 2025-03-07.
